machine state cleanup requires an agreed allow bit; ordinary owner cleanup remains usable
AUTH_SYS and authentication-only GSS cannot negotiate machine protection; SP4_NONE implicit binding remains available
one context shared across 32 sessions and three TCP paths admits only its 64-entry RPC window; completing the oldest request releases the next authenticated callback
krb5/krb5i/krb5p CB_NULL, CB_SEQUENCE and CB_NOTIFY_LOCK use real Kerberos, independent RPC counters and exact referring calls; notifications grant no lock
BACKCHANNEL_CTL rejects unknown handles/invalid services/oversized RPC credentials atomically; existing handles are idempotent and counters never reset
BACKCHANNEL_CTL adds handles instead of replacing them; empty additions retain GSS, and destruction of another context preserves the live path
sixteen live callback tuples are bounded; exhaustion preserves the existing channel and duplicate offers consume no extra capacity
negotiated channel sizes include exact GSS credential, MIC and wrapped-body overhead; exact request limits succeed and one-byte-short channels send no oversized callbacks
unsigned, bad MIC/ciphertext and wrong authenticated sequences cannot complete callbacks; disconnect/rebind retries exact CB_SEQUENCE plaintext with fresh RPC authentication
nearly expired and expired contexts set SEQUENCE flags; expiry/destroy removes path authority without AUTH_NONE fallback, and fresh contexts restore it
CREATE_SESSION binds a bidirectional transport; CB_NULL uses the requested program/version and AUTH_NONE while forechannel RPC stays usable
probe replies are bound to their exact TCP connection and XID; cross-connection, duplicate and unknown replies cannot change path state
BACKCHANNEL_CTL changes program and invalidates old probes; malformed matched replies keep path down and idempotent rebinding reprobes it
cleared callback credentials and destroyed/recreated sessions cannot be validated by a stale probe response
BIND_CONN_TO_SESSION supports BACK and BACK_OR_BOTH on new transports, rejects invalid directions and changes to existing channel roles
AUTH_SYS CB_NULL carries the offered timestamp, machine name, UID/GID and supplementary groups exactly
five-second probe timeout ignores late success; rebind recovers the path without recreating the session
losing the only callback transport sets CB_PATH_DOWN on a surviving forechannel connection
CB_NULL success alone does not validate the sequenced backchannel; CB_SEQUENCE success on the wrong transport is ignored
truncated/trailing XDR, bad status/tag/count/op/session/sequence/slot and CB_SEQUENCE errors close the transport before exact retry; only a valid reply advances the slot
successful CB_SEQUENCE advances exactly once; BACKCHANNEL_CTL retains the session sequence and ignores old duplicate replies
BIND and callback program replacement never retry an outstanding CB_COMPOUND on a live transport; its original reply releases the slot without validating the new program
completion of a callback issued before credential removal advances its slot but cannot resurrect the disabled backchannel
CB_COMPOUND timeout closes the original transport before retry; stale RPC replies on the replacement cannot complete the unresolved slot
one callback slot serializes multiple bound paths; transport loss retries the unresolved request on another bound connection
loss of the only backchannel with an unanswered CB_COMPOUND reports CB_PATH_DOWN_SESSION; binding a replacement clears that flag and preserves the pending sequence
client-advertised slot growth beyond CREATE_SESSION and shrink back to zero are accepted without allocation or increasing callback concurrency
destroying and recreating a session starts a distinct callback slot at sequence one; old CB_COMPOUND success cannot validate it
UINT32_MAX offered callback slots require only slot zero; AUTH_SYS credentials must fit the negotiated complete CB_COMPOUND request size
four backchannel offers preserve operation/concurrency counts and never increase buffer/RDMA limits; forechannel stays bounded
CREATE_SESSION retries preserve the original negotiated session; subsequent SEQUENCE/GETFH and explicit destruction work
AUTH_SYS machine-protection negotiation is denied per operation; the same owner can establish an ordinary SP4_NONE client afterward
OPEN advertises MAY_NOTIFY_LOCK; READW conflict release delivers exact handle/owner/referring request; the hint neither grants nor reserves the lock
nonblocking LOCK denial does not enroll a waiter and cancels a previous blocking request for the same owner/file
closing the waiting OPEN removes its unsent notification without granting lock state
fresh write-policy authority is required before dispatch; revocation drops the waiter and restoring rights does not resurrect it
inconsistent operation status and lost notification reply cause disconnect then exact two-operation replay; RETRY_UNCACHED_REP consumes the slot without granting a lock
multiple waiting owners share one bounded callback slot and no second notification is sent before the first completes
client NOTSUPP completes the optional callback; foreground polling and explicit lock acquisition remain usable
two-operation callbacks respect negotiated operation and full RPC size limits; constrained clients can still poll for locks
expired client and OPEN state remove the queued hint; releasing the competing lock never notifies or revives the expired session
